_readme: Wan 3.0 on Higgsfield and fal. Since 2026-11-27 an option priced beside Seedance 2.5 on every micro-drama quote (owner: 'this is how we're going to scale ai video'). The house mode for dialogue clips is REFERENCE mode: character, place and product sheets as image references, one voice sample per speaker, an optional silent camera rehearsal; native audio on; 480p 9:16. The start-frame route below stays for single silent shots.

SOURCES ARE FLAGGED [official] / [vendor] / [anecdotal] / [own test]. Alibaba publishes an official Wan 3.0 prompt guide (sources); limits read live from fal's schema and `higgsfield model get wan3_0` on 2026-11-27. Every rule is draft until a paid take proves it (tests: the open list).

THE FACTS THAT SHAPE THE DOOR: a start or end picture never travels with references, so reference mode rebuilds the first frame from the sheets; references are named Image N / Video N / Audio N by upload order within each type; there is no negative-prompt field; the prompt may be rewritten by the vendor.
No brand, product, person or format word appears in this file.

limits.smart_duration: -1 lets the model choose the length; the door always sends a number
limits.start_and_references: start_image / end_image cannot be combined with image, video or audio references on this door
limits.price_per_second_usd: 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.20 (480p / 720p / 1080p) on the keyed API, fal and Alibaba

house.role: an option on every micro-drama quote, picked at the owner's go (2026-11-27); Seedance 2.5 stays the default when he names none
house.mode: reference mode: each speaker's sheet, the place sheet, the product sheet as image references; one voice sample per speaker; optional silent camera rehearsal as Video 1
house.resolution: 480p, then the house's own upscale or phone pass
house.duration: the shot list's length, 4-15 s typical
house.voice_budget: 15 s across all samples: two speakers about 5-7 s each, three about 4-5 s each
house.takes: one take, another only on failure
house.start_frame_route: image-to-video from one approved start picture, sound off: single silent shots only

limits.reference_mode: Reference mode (reference pictures + voices + motion video, no start picture) is the mode a continuous take uses: the picture rides as a reference, so the first frame is rebuilt from it, not copied.

fal_route.enable_safety_checker: false turns off fal's own checker only; the vendor still moderates the model ('model_moderated', read 2026-11-09)
fal_route.read: 2026-11-09, fal openapi schema and two live calls

limits.start_frame_mode: A start picture with no references: the exact first frame and the script; the model speaks every line in its own voices (our reads are laid after). Takes a first frame in bikinis on Higgsfield (2026-11-09).
limits.higgsfield_cli_media_flags: --start-image, --image-references, --audio-references, --video-references; repeat a flag for several files; local paths are uploaded
limits.image_rule: jpg/jpeg/png (no transparency)/bmp/webp, 240-8000 px a side, aspect within 8:1, 20 MB each [official]
limits.video_rule: mp4/mov, 1-15 s each, 15 s total, at least 16 fps, input + output at most 30 s, input seconds billed [official][vendor fal]
limits.audio_rule: wav/mp3, 1-15 s each, 15 s total, 15 MB each [official]

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.what: Overall line, reference block, timed shot list, dialogue, sound, style, negatives, in that order (structure: formula-order).
inputs.allowed: up to 20,000 characters; attention narrows past a few hundred words [vendor runware]

inputs.name: start_image
inputs.what: The approved first picture; the clip starts on it.
inputs.we_send: none in reference mode; the approved picture on the start-frame route

inputs.name: end_image
inputs.what: A last picture the clip settles on.
inputs.we_send: only when the shot has its own last picture

inputs.name: image_references / video_references / audio_references
inputs.what: Image N = sheets (face, build, clothing; the place; the product), Audio N = one voice sample per speaker, Video N = a silent camera rehearsal; numbered by upload order within each type.
inputs.allowed: images up to 10, videos up to 5 (15 s, billed), audio up to 5 (15 s); 20 in all
inputs.we_send: each speaker's sheet, then the place, then the product (3-6); one voice sample per speaker in speaker order; the camera rehearsal when the shot needs it

inputs.name: generate_audio
inputs.we_send: true in reference mode (native speech, effects, room sound); false on the silent start-frame route

inputs.name: enable_thinking
inputs.we_send: test on and off (the Studio's fal call sends true today); the effect is unmeasured

inputs.name: enable_prompt_expansion (fal) / prompt_extend (Alibaba)
inputs.what: An LLM rewrites the prompt before generation.
inputs.allowed: default true; not exposed on Higgsfield
inputs.we_send: test false on fal to keep exact lines and timestamps; read actual_prompt when true
inputs.source: [vendor fal] off may lower quality; [vendor comfy] off for exact wording; [anecdotal eachlabs] can blur timestamps

structure.rule: With a start picture, say it is the first frame and describe only what changes: the action and the camera.
structure.ours: the house clip prompt opens 'Image 1 is the first frame'

structure.rule: Say the camera keeps the first frame's framing; left unsaid, the first take pushed in from full body to waist-up within a second.
structure.ours: the door adds a framing line to every prompt

structure.rule: One action per shot, written as visible movement.
Overall description, reference citations, shots with timestamps (subject, place, move, camera), dialogue, sound, style and mood, negative list. Leave out a section the clip does not need.
Name references 'Image N', 'Video N', 'Audio N', counted by upload order within each type; with two or more of a type always use the number.
structure.source: [official] API reference and guide; '@Image1' is one vendor's form, untested here

structure.rule: Say what each reference gives and nothing more: 'Image 1 is <name>, one <man|woman>, a character sheet: face, hair, skin, build and clothing only'; 'Image 3 is the room: layout and light only; nobody from it appears'; 'Video 1 is used only for camera movement; take no people, look or sound from it'.
structure.source: [official] guide: say what each material is for, or features bleed between subjects

structure.rule: One 'Subject locking: <name> Image N, ...' line; restate each person's key traits in the shots; 'consistent throughout' and 'they do not look alike'.
Once per speaker: '<Name>'s voice timbre references Audio N, <register>'; take only the voice characteristics and have the person say the lines below.
structure.source: [official] guide; register in the binding carried over from the Drama Ads Seedance findings [own]

structure.rule: Each line inside its shot: '<Name> says (<delivery in face and voice words>): "<exact words>"' then 'Lip sync.' Name the speaker on every line; never two speakers' lines in one sentence.
After the shots: 'Only the quoted lines are spoken, word for word, in <language>, each once, by the named speaker; no other speech.' A shot with no lines says 'No one speaks in this shot.'
structure.source: [official] say 'no dialogue' or it may add some; the language line is an untested Seedance lesson [own]

structure.rule: 'Shot N [a-bs]:' windows that touch, 2-5 s each, one bracket style throughout, each ending 'Hard cut.'; 'One continuous shot.' on the first line for a single take. No fast repeated actions.
structure.source: [official] guide; [own test] 2026-11-09: a 3-shot list cut in one call, shot 3 framed the wrong two people

structure.rule: A 'Fixed spatial relationships:' line: who stands left or right, by what landmark, and that nobody crosses.

Shot size, angle and ONE named move per shot in plain words (handheld follow, push in, pull out, whip pan, snap zoom, orbit, tracking, tilt); no stacked moves. Fits the drama camera recipe: a move in every shot, a cut every 2-3 s.
Name the room sound and the action sounds in their own sentence and write 'no background music'.

No negative field exists: end the prompt with 'Negative prompt list:' and only the real risks (subtitles, on-screen text, watermark, a third person, twins or duplicate faces, costume change, face drift, background music).
structure.source: [official] guide; fal and Higgsfield schemas carry no negative_prompt

structure.rule: 150-300 words; few beats for the seconds, or the end compresses or drops.

avoid.text: Sending reference pictures, clips or sound together with a start picture: the door refuses the mix.
Leaving generated sound on: it is on by default.
Naming a real person, brand or franchise in the prompt: the vendor's moderation checks prompts, pictures and the finished clip.
Expecting it to speak our locked voice read from a start picture: on this door a start picture cannot carry audio.
Prompt words that call Image 1 the first frame in reference mode: no frame travels with references, so the model may paste a sheet in as the opening.
A reference picture with more than one person or a busy background, or one reference doing two jobs.
A storyboard or multi-panel picture with no line saying it is shot guidance only: it is read as one frame.
Style labels like a genre name that can turn into on-screen text: describe the look instead.
Two voice samples close in pitch and pace: they blur into one voice.
Two angles of one moment made as two calls: the scene is rebuilt differently; cut them inside one call.

history.about: Wan 3.0 added to the house as a person's pick for clips, run on the Higgsfield plan's credits
Wan 3.0 is an option on every micro-drama quote, the way to scale AI video; reference-mode prompt rules added from Alibaba's official guide, start-frame rules kept for single silent shots

tests.what: a 20 s continuous take of a three-person scene, reference mode, two voice samples (4.8 s and 6.1 s), 20 credits on Higgsfield
tests.result: the subject walks the line and the handheld camera follows; 9 of 10 lines spoken, one word dropped; a motion video reference was refused by the plan's content filter

tests.what: start-frame mode, 20 s, a written one-take scene (two women walk a line of three men feeling each man's cheeks)
tests.result: both takes walked the line and spoke all 10 lines in order, 20 credits each; our reads laid after matched the speaking moments

camera.control: take.py `camera` (move, angle, framing), a line's own `camera` per beat, `shots` (a shot list cut inside one call), `views` (the same moment once per view, cut line by line); camera control runs on Wan 3.0 and Seedance 2.5 only (ruled 2026-11-09)
camera.multi_cam_views: tested 2026-11-09 on Wan 3.0 reference mode (fal), 2 views x 20 s, 2 USD: the cut runs on unbroken words, but two separate calls rebuild the scene differently (the men swap places and one changes face between views), so the views do not match; a model's own shot list inside one call keeps the people and places
camera.start_frame_per_beat: [own test 2026-11-09, Higgsfield CLI start-frame mode, 10 s, 10 credits, job a82258b5-35c5-4b8c-b348-39732b2ed6f6] a camera line per beat is followed in order inside one continuous take: starts wide on the line-up, pushes in fast to a close-up on the hands on the first man's jaw, pans right to the second man, holds a two-shot; the exact first frame is kept
camera.reference_shot_list: [own test 2026-11-09, fal reference mode, 10 s, 0.50 USD, request 01a1bf20-0ad0-7201-8152-e6877bf7f032] a shot list (Shot 1 0-3 s wide, Shot 2 3-7 s over-the-shoulder close-up, Shot 3 7-10 s low two-shot) is cut inside one call: wide, then over-the-shoulder close on the speaker, then a low two-shot; the third shot framed two different people than asked
camera.angle: in start-frame mode the first frame fixes the opening angle; a new angle comes from a move (push, pan, swing) or a cut in the shot list

open_tests.test: 4 s, 1 sheet, 1 voice sample whose words differ from the quoted line
open_tests.look_for: the new line in the sample's voice, none of the sample's own words

open_tests.test: 4 s, Audio 1 is the exact line's recording, prompt says lip-sync to Audio 1
open_tests.look_for: our recording played (an exact locked voice) or a new read

open_tests.test: the worked two-speaker clip at 6 s, then the voice uploads swapped with the prompt unchanged
open_tests.look_for: each line stays in the voice its binding names, from the right mouth
the right face on the right name and line

open_tests.test: fal: prompt expansion on and off; Higgsfield once
open_tests.look_for: lines word for word, cuts near their timestamps; Higgsfield's behaviour

open_tests.test: thinking on and off, everything else the same
open_tests.look_for: who is in frame in the last shot, dropped words, cut timing

open_tests.test: with and without the negative and sound lines
open_tests.look_for: music on a spectrogram, subtitles in frames
twins, face drift, a third person

open_tests.test: a silent 4 s 3D rehearsal as Video 1, camera only, on Higgsfield
open_tests.look_for: the camera follows it, nothing of the stand-ins carried, no refusal
how far cuts and lines land from their seconds, a dropped ending, a repeated last line

open_tests.test: the same 8 s prompt with 3 images, then 10

example_reference_mode:
Overall: one 8-second vertical live-action micro-drama scene in three shots with hard cuts, handheld phone-camera realism, tension that turns. Two people in frame in every shot.

References: Image 1 is <A>, one man, a character sheet: use it only for his face, hair, skin, build and clothing. Image 2 is <B>, one woman, a character sheet: use it only for her face, hair, skin, build and clothing. Image 3 is the kitchen: use it only for the room, its layout and its light; nobody from Image 3 appears.
<A>'s voice timbre references Audio 1, a low, calm male voice. <B>'s voice timbre references Audio 2, a bright, quick female voice. Take only the voice characteristics from each audio and have each person say the lines below.
Subject locking: <A> Image 1, <B> Image 2, kitchen Image 3. Each keeps their own face, hair, build and clothing, consistent throughout; they do not look alike.
Fixed spatial relationships: <A> stands at the counter on the left, <B> stands in the doorway on the right; nobody crosses.

Shot 1 [0-3s]: medium two-shot at eye level, handheld push in from the doorway toward the counter. <A> turns from the counter to <B>, brows pulled together, mouth tight. <A> says (low, flat): "You told her before you told me?" Lip sync. Hard cut.
Shot 2 [3-5.5s]: close-up on <B> over <A>'s shoulder; handheld whip pan onto her. Her eyes drop to the floor, then lift to him; she exhales. <B> says (quiet and quick): "I didn't know how to tell you." Lip sync. Hard cut.
Shot 3 [5.5-8s]: low two-shot from the counter, handheld orbit a quarter turn to the right. <A> sets his mug down; <B> takes one step toward him and stops. No one speaks in this shot.

Dialogue: only the two quoted lines are spoken, word for word, in American English, each once, by the named speaker; no other speech.
Sound: kitchen room tone and the mug on the counter; no background music.
Style: natural phone-video realism, warm practical kitchen light.
Negative prompt list: subtitles, on-screen text, watermark, a third person, twins or duplicate faces, costume change, face drift, background music.
